title: docs(guide): continuous 4-axis walkthrough on the Tormach 770MX + microARC 4
body:
**Stacked on #2342** (`issue/796-tormach-wrapped-a`, Fixes #796). This branch starts from that PR's head `ef864e37d`; until #2342 merges, this PR's diff also shows its files. It merges after #2342. Fork synced at upstream main 4e8616b (through #2342's branch).

## What changed

The continuous half of #1904: a step-by-step guide page for the Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, with a committed demo project and drawn pictures.

- **Page:** `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-continuous-4axis-part.md`, "Your first continuous 4-axis program". It covers: how the bar is held; the machine file's four A values (axis, travel, `nose_to_axis`, A rate) and what to compare with the machine; finding the A centreline and setting G54 on it; the ball tool; a Rotary Parallel operation, setting by setting; the checks and what the stock simulation says; the posted program read line by line; what the post refuses; a run in the PathPilot simulator; then a single-block start and an air cut with no bar.
- **What the post writes, in plain words, from the Hub readings on #796:** `G93` on a feed that turns A with X Y Z, and why (reading 2: in `G94` F is the X Y Z distance only; reading 3: `G93` is accepted and timed); the A rate cap worked out on real lines; an A-only feed in `G94` with F in degrees per minute (reading 4); A counting on through 180 (reading 1); `G94` back before the last rapid.
- **Demo project:** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`, the program it posts `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` (3213 lines) and the model `examples/models/first-continuous-4axis-part.obj` (made by `gen_first_continuous_4axis_part_obj.py`). #2342's kit project was not reused: it has no continuous operation, and its wrap golden has a stock that ends where the model ends.
- **Pictures:** three SVG files in `site/static/guide-pictures/`, drawn from the committed project, model and program by `site/tools/first_continuous_4axis_pictures.py`: the bar and the work offset, each move unrolled (X against A), and the A word line by line with the G93 lines marked. No PNG, no screenshot. The UI renderer of #1902 (PR #2078) is not merged, so there are no UI renders yet.
- **Links and corrections:** linked from Getting started, First run, "Your first 4-axis part", the Multi-axis index and "Continuous 4-axis". `continuous-4-axis.md` no longer says that no shipped post writes inverse-time feed, and the Multi-axis index no longer says that `tormach.cps` indexes A only (both untrue since #2342). `continuous-4-axis.md` has a new section "End faces and the chuck".
- `docs/decisions/1904-continuous-4axis-walkthrough.md`.

## Two findings that shape the page

1. **The page ends with an air cut and tells the reader not to cut.** Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model down to the axis. On a bar held in a chuck, the chuck-side end face is inside the bar: the program feeds to Z-0.03 at X-1.3125 while the stock goes on to X-2. With a 1/2 in flute the shank check blocks the post (good); with a longer flute it posts with no warning. No setting keeps the pass off an end face. Filed as **#2343**. The page says this at the top, in "Check it" and at the end.
2. **Rotary Offset cannot be used on this machine file.** Each level that cuts takes two laps of A, and the post refuses the count past -360..360. Filed as **#2344**.

This is a partial delivery for #1904. The wrapped engraving or slot is unavailable. Neither program has a recorded PathPilot Hub run to M30. The guide describes an air cut, but no Hub run or machine run was done. Keep #1904 open for this acceptance work.

## Review fixes

Inherited parent #2342 head `b93fe06131248f91e41e90104e0d050409add852` with a merge commit. Its feed-time calculation bounds the curved part-relative trajectory from the rounded posted words. The parent includes an independent trajectory pin. This child refreshes its example program for that safety correction. The guide now explains the curved trajectory bound. Its four excerpts, stated line numbers, feed calculations and generated SVG pictures remain valid without numeric changes.

Both NC comparisons allow tightly bounded platform rounding differences. The comparisons preserve line structure and exact nonnumeric words. The independent rate checks remain. The committed program refresh is required by the inherited safety fix, rather than used to hide platform differences.

This partial delivery uses `Refs #1904`. The issue stays open for the missing Hub runs to M30 and the wrapped engraving or slot.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/796-tormach-wrapped-a`: green (app suite `continuous_4axis_part`, 5 tests):
  - `the_continuous_4axis_part_posts_its_wrapped_program`: the committed project is byte for byte the built document; G93 on each feed that turns A with X Y Z and on no other move; A never jumps; A inside the travel
  - `the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program`: loads with no notes, passes the machine check and the post gate
  - `each_g93_move_holds_the_a_rate`
  - `the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline` (the fact behind "air cut only")
  - `a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test continuous_4axis_part -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests`: the 13 new tests of `test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py` pass (UI labels in their sources, tables against the project, G-code excerpts as runs of the program, stated line numbers and A range, quoted refusals in the post, pictures equal to the script's output, links). 46 of 49 pass. The 3 failures are the same on the unchanged base (`test_first_4axis_part ... test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones`, `test_guide_icons` x2) and are filed as #2345.
- `zola check` in `site/`: 45 pages, no broken link.

title: feat(post): wrapped A on the Tormach microARC 4 (G93, cumulative A)
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` no longer refuses an A that changes inside an operation on an A-about-X machine. It now posts it as wrapped (simultaneous) A, based on mkinney's four PathPilot Hub readings on #796 (v2.14.4, 770MX SIM, 4th axis on):

- **A is cumulative.** PathPilot treats A as plain degrees with no rollover (A350 -> `G1 A10` turned back 340 deg). Each target is the nearest equivalent of the held angle: 179 -> 181, 359 -> 361, never back through 0. A count past the stated travel is refused by name.
- **A turning X Y Z feed is G93.** `F = 1 / t`, where t (min) = max((the tip's path relative to the part + one rounding step) / the programmed feed, the posted |dA| / the stated A rate). F is floored to 0.001, so rounding only ever slows a move. Neither the cutting feed nor the A rate is exceeded. The rate comes from `rotaryRate` (#885).
- **An A-only feed stays G94**, with F in deg/min under the same time law (Hub reading 4). Feeds that don't turn A are unchanged. G94 is restated before any motion that is not a G93 feed and at every section end.
- **Turning moves are split onto their segment.** The machine moves XYZ in a line while A turns, so the tip relative to the part bows off the stream's segment. Each turning move (rapids too) is split into 2^k pieces until the bow is within 0.005 mm (at most 256 pieces, else refused by name).
- **A is reset between operations:** as before (#785), each section restates its first A as -180..180 after `G53 G0 Z0`, so a wrap that ended at A300 unwinds at the top of Z.
- **Refused by name:** a machine file with no A rate ("states no A feed rate"), a count past the travel ("A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over)"), an arc / canned cycle / probe move that would turn A, a turning move from an unknown start, and a move that still bows after 256 splits.
- `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` now states A `max_normal_speed` 360 deg/min. That is the rate the Hub ran as asked. It is conservative: no Tormach rate could be cited with confidence.
- Docs: the tester-kit README, `first-4axis-part.md` and `continuous-4-axis.md` (with its site test), plus `docs/decisions/796-tormach-wrapped-a.md`. The kit's `.camproj` was re-saved by its own test, so it carries the A rate.

Fork branch based on upstream `main` at 4e8616b (not a cut tag), so the #885 rule and the current post are in.

## How tested

New pins in `crates/app/tests/tormach_wrapped_a.rs` (10 tests):
- `a_long_xyz_move_takes_its_time_from_the_feed`: `G93 G1 X50 Y0 Z0 A1 F11.999` (50 mm at F600)
- `a_mostly_rotary_move_takes_its_time_from_the_a_rate`: `G1 X51 Y0 Z0 A91 F4` (90 deg at 360 deg/min)
- `g94_comes_back_before_an_xyz_only_feed_and_a_turns_in_deg_per_min`
- `a_counts_on_through_180_and_360_never_back_through_0`
- `the_next_operation_resets_a_at_the_safe_z`
- `a_section_that_ends_in_g93_restates_g94_before_m5`
- `a_turning_move_off_the_axis_is_split_onto_its_chord`: every posted point, turned back into the part, lies on the stream's chord, and each piece is held to both rates
- `a_count_past_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`, `a_machine_with_no_a_rate_is_refused_by_name`, `the_microarc_states_its_a_rate`

Golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc` is the microARC kit's job plus a real Rotary Parallel (1/8" ball) on the bar. It is pinned by `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, which replaces `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_is_refused_by_name` and also checks A unwrapping, G93 on every turning XYZ feed, G94 elsewhere, and G94 at the section end.

Updated: `tormach_fourth_axis::an_a_that_changes_inside_an_operation_posts_wrapped_a` (was `..._is_refused`). In `fourth_axis_pose`, the two fanuc tests on the microARC file now place A with a rapid first, because that file now states an A rate and the #885 rule asks for it. The recorded `rotary.refusal` golden for tormach (tilt-head machine) now names the B tilt refusal instead.

Gate (macOS, debug, targeted - `cargo xtask gate quick` plans every app suite because a new golden is shared test input, so the touched suites ran instead): every camcraft-app test binary that names Tormach / the microARC (69 binaries, incl. `tormach_wrapped_a`, `microarc_test_part`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `first_4axis_part`, `index_swing`, `tormach_post`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `recorded_post_streams`) and every camcraft-post binary that names Tormach or the recorded streams (45 binaries, incl. `script_tormach`, `explain_tormach`, `recorded_streams`): all green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app` on the four changed test files `-D warnings`: clean. `site/tests/test_first_4axis_part.py`: the updated tests pass; `test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones` fails the same way on upstream main (machine name not in `posting.rs`), not touched here.

## Not exercised

- No real cut, and this exact program has not been run in the Hub. The readings cover single test moves only.
- PathPilot's A soft limits. The file keeps -360..360, and a wrap past it is refused.

## Hub check (before trusting it on the 770MX + microARC 4)

Run slowly (feed override 25-50 %, single block for the first lines), with the tool lifted 1" above the work offset (air cut):
1. Post the golden's WRAP op (or `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) and load it in the Hub 770MX SIM with the 4th axis on. Confirm it loads with no error on `G93` / `G94` lines and no "F word missing".
2. Watch the A DRO on a stretch that passes 180 (e.g. line 1393 of the golden, A180 -> A185.757): A must keep counting up, never swing back through 0.
3. Time one long G93 line against its F (time = 1/F min). Check one A-only `G1 A.. F360` runs at 6 deg/s.
4. Confirm the control is back in G94 after the WRAP op (Status tab / the next op's feeds run at their ipm).
5. Check PathPilot's A soft limits (jog A past +360 / -360 in the SIM) and report them on #796, so the machine file's travel can be stated.
6. Only then air-cut on the real machine at a low override, the bar in the chuck, a hand on feed hold.

Changelog: Tormach PathPilot post: continuous (wrapped) A on the microARC 4 - A counts on past 360, turning feeds in G93 held to the feed and the stated A rate (360 deg/min); refused by name when the machine states no A rate or the count passes the A travel (#796)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #796

title: perf(ui): cache the shown operation status on a world write revision
body:
This PR is stacked on #2331. Its base is `issue/2201-frame-caches`. Retarget it to `main` before #2331 merges.

## What changed

Cost row 1 of #2201. The UI computed `operation::status_of` (the full generation stamp) for each operation on each frame. This now occurs only when the world changes.

- `schema::WorldRevision` and `app::world_rev` (new). Two flecs observers move one revision on each `OnAdd`, `OnSet` and `OnRemove` of each component. One observer is for the wildcard id and one is for the wildcard pair. Each move takes a fresh number from one process counter, so two worlds never share a value. The read-time memos `GeoSig` and `GeomPrintMemo` do not move it.
- `operation::status_shown` and `operation::stale_reason_shown` (new, `status_memo.rs`). These keep the answer of `status_of` / `stale_reason` for each operation until the revision moves.
- These UI readers use the cached reader:
  - the browser tree row
  - the stale count in the status bar (`panes.rs`)
  - the operation page status and stale reason
  - the debug panel
- These callers keep `status_of`, the uncached truth:
  - generation
  - verify
  - the collision checks
  - the post, `posting_sim` and the post dialog
  - `RegenerateAll`
  - MCP and the script API
- `SetSetupPostScriptOptions` wrote `SetupDef` in place (`get::<&mut SetupDef>`). That write sends no event. It now clones and `set`s.
- Row 7: `op_page.rs`, `state.rs` and `shell.rs` read the toolpath through `model::with_toolpath`. They do not clone it.

## The key and its writers

`status_of` reads only world components. Each writer of these components uses `set`, `add`, `remove` or `destruct`. Thus the observer covers each writer:

- each command `apply` and `invert` (undo and redo)
- the generation result and `ClearToolpath`
- the verify results (in `Toolpath.warnings`)
- the tool, stock, setup, machine and model edits
- project load (into the same world or a new world)
- entity delete

The decision file `docs/decisions/2201-status-cache.md` has the full table. The test `no_component_is_written_in_place` scans `app` and `ui` and fails on a new in-place component write (`&mut` terms, `ensure_mut`, `get_mut::<`).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/status_cache.rs` (10 tests):
  - `still_frames_compute_each_status_once` (the build count)
  - `reads_never_move_the_revision`
  - `an_operation_param_edit_rebuilds_and_undo_redo_follow`
  - `a_tool_edit_and_a_tool_delete_rebuild`
  - `generate_and_clear_rebuild`
  - `stock_model_and_placement_edits_rebuild`
  - `a_prior_operation_edit_rebuilds_the_next_one`
  - `setup_machine_and_delete_rebuild`
  - `a_project_load_rebuilds`
  - `no_component_is_written_in_place`
  - Each test also asserts that the cached value equals `status_of` and `stale_reason`.
  - Mutation check: with the observer store disabled, 6 of the tests fail.
- `frame_cost_ops_probe`: still frames with 1 and 8 operations compute no status (`statuses: 0` for f1, f8, g8 and n8).

## Readings (debug, fig8.step, 6 still frames, `frame_cost_ops_probe`)

| State | ui before | ui after | scene before | scene after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f1 one toolpath, selected | 8.68 ms | 2.46 ms | 2.67 ms | 2.40 ms |
| f8 eight toolpaths, one selected | 12.10 ms | 2.59 ms | 2.72 ms | 2.59 ms |
| g8 eight toolpaths, all shown | 12.78 ms | 2.65 ms | 3.24 ms | 2.89 ms |
| n8 eight toolpaths, none selected | 11.30 ms | 1.85 ms | 2.54 ms | 2.34 ms |

In f1, `ui/browser` went from 3.43 to 0.53 ms. `ui/status` went from 2.89 to 0.06 ms. In f8, `ui/browser` went from 5.24 to 0.68 ms, and `ui/status` went from 4.30 to 0.06 ms.

## Gates (debug, `-j 4`)

- app tests:
  - `status_cache` 10
  - `commands_undo` 30
  - `post_script_options` 7
  - `operations` 120
  - `project_roundtrip` 73
  - `setups` 12
  - `stock_stamp` 4
  - All pass.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 1024 pass, 6 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Release timings.
- The GUI exe (not started).
- The `crates/ui/tests/` integration binaries.
- The MCP and script paths (unchanged, they call `status_of`).
- Snapshot PNGs (not changed).

Effort: high

Changelog: The operation tree, status bar and operation page no longer compute each operation's status again on each frame. A still frame with eight operations draws the UI about four times faster.

Refs #2201

title: fix(setup-align): accept 2D Chamfer in a setup that holds the part turned
body:
## What changed
- `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs`: `verified_kind` accepts `OpParams::Chamfer2D`. The refusal message lists 2D Chamfer with the verified kinds. No generator code changes.
- New proof test file `crates/app/tests/setup_align_chamfer.rs`.
- `setup_align.rs`, `opframe_picks.rs` and `setup_align_2d_kinds.rs` tests used 2D Chamfer as the example of a refused kind. They use Deburr (#2284) now, because Deburr stays refused.
- Decision file `docs/decisions/2283-aligned-chamfer.md`.

## Why the kind is safe
2D Chamfer reads the same doors as 2D Contour:
- the picked region comes from `region_for_job` (picks through `OpFrame::pose_in_setup`);
- the machine area is the section of the setup-frame material (`material_source`);
- the top plane resolves through the shared height law.

The refusal stayed only because no proof test existed (the rule of #2276).

## Readings (pinning tests)
`turned_chamfer_cuts_like_the_baked_part`:
- The fixture is an L prism. The setup turns it 90 degrees about X, then 90 degrees about Z. The tool is `CM-0600-90`, 1 mm at 45 degrees, top plane `TopOfModel`.
- The source is ONE picked edge on the face that is up in the setup frame. `operation::extend_to_loop_in` closes it to the loop of that face.
- The turned setup and the part with the turn baked into its facets cut the same moves (to 1e-6 mm). The two verify clean, simulate with 0 gouge cells, and post the same program.
- The coordinates agree with the aligned geometry: the turned top face is X [10, 20], Y [-5, 5] at Z 15. Each cut is within the tool radius of that square and no deeper than 3 mm below Z 15. The ride is a square centred on (15, 0).
- The part as modelled cuts a different path.

`unaligned_chamfer_rides_the_modelled_top`: in an unaligned setup, `generation_problem` returns `None`, and the ride rings the L top at Z 10 as before.

Red on the old code: `turned_chamfer_cuts_like_the_baked_part` failed with `setup 'Setup1' holds the part turned (part alignment) - 2D Chamfer is not supported yet in an aligned setup (...)`. `unaligned_chamfer_rides_the_modelled_top` passed on the old code too (the unaligned program does not change).

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick` on head f9904306767348db491d83a5e4d016c881577415: 810 steps, 0 failed, clippy `-D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised
- No GUI session ran. The edge pick and the loop extension are tested through `extend_to_loop_in`, not through the viewport.
- Only one turn (90 degrees about X and Z) and one convex face loop are tested. No inside chamfer (bore edge) in a turned setup is tested.
- A tilted plane in an aligned setup stays refused, as before.

Changelog: 2D Chamfer now generates in a setup that holds the part turned (part alignment), instead of a refusal.

title: fix(ui): cache toolpath overlay lines and the solid box per input (#2201)
body:
## What changed

This PR takes over the work of PR #2256 by its author, by the decision of the maintainer on 2026-11-17. The branch of PR #2256 is not changed. The measurements of PR #2256 showed where to look; thanks to its author.

The viewport built two values again on each frame. The cost grew with the operation count. This PR caches the two values. Each key holds the real inputs, not `doc_version` alone (docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md).

The cause is the dive start. The verify reading is correct.

- A bore-side contour cuts only its ring. It does not cut the core inside the ring.

- The new function `column_top` gives the material top at the dive point. It is the plane above when the point is on the cut path, or when an earlier plunge opened that column. Else it is the top of the material.
- The substituted dive and the Plunge arm use this value for the rapid height.
- Later levels keep the short rapid over the plane above, because the first dive opened the column.

title: fix(post): judge a document with no machine against the default machine's limits
body:
## What changed

- The program gate now judges the operations of each mount with no machine against the limits of the default machine file (`3axis-vmc.mch`). The post writes these operations with that file, so the gate reads the same values.
- The gate judges two limits: the spindle speed range and the feed rate of each linear axis. These are the same checks that a mounted machine gets, in the same words.
- The refusal names the default machine, each operation and each limit. It tells the user to mount a machine on the setup or to change the operation.
- `posting::default_limits` reads the limits from the default file. The file uses the post grammar (`kinematics.static`), so `parse_mch` cannot read it. A zero, negative or absent number is unstated and checks nothing.
- If the default file does not read, the gate refuses by the file name and names the setups (#2319).
- A mounted machine is judged by its own file only, as before. The status line machine vote does not change.
- The new code is in `crates/app/src/posting_default_machine.rs`. `posting_mounts.rs` gets one call. `posting.rs` changes one `pub use` line and does not grow.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2321-default-machine-limits.md`.

## Readings on the code before the fix

- An operation at 7000 mm/min posted with no refusal. The default X/Y rate is 5000 mm/min.
- An operation at 15000 rpm was refused only by the engine warning `spindle rpm over machine maximum`. That text names no operation and no limit. The gate now refuses it first, by name.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/default_machine_limits.rs`:
- `no_mounted_machine_is_refused_above_the_default_spindle_maximum` (red before the fix)
- `no_mounted_machine_is_refused_above_the_default_feed_rate` (red before the fix: the program posted)

- `a_mounted_machine_is_judged_by_its_own_file_only` (a mounted machine with no stated limits posts 15000 rpm and 7000 mm/min, as before)
- `the_default_limits_are_read_from_the_post_grammar`

Red proof: with the gate clause removed, the three marked tests fail. The other three pass. `default_machine_missing` (9 tests, #2319) passes.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick`, 810 steps, 0 failed, clippy clean.

## Not exercised

- The GUI. The status line vote is not changed.
- Pose and rotary laws for the default machine. The default file states no rotaries, but this change adds no pose check for documents with no machine (see the decision file).
- Release-tier heavy lanes.

Changelog: A document with no mounted machine is now refused when an operation exceeds the default machine's spindle speed or feed rate; the refusal names the operation and the limit.

title: fix(3d): prevent shared-depth XY crossings in adaptive microlifts, helices, and offset shells
body:
## What changed

- Landed `entry::helix_about`'s final half-turn on exact `z1` and clamped intermediate `lattice` depths monotonically toward `z1` ([entry.rs](crates/motion/src/entry.rs)).
- Extracted shared depth-overlap and `CROSSING_TOUCH = 1e-9` segment-crossing checks (`z_depths_overlap`, `proper_cross_touch`, `seg_crosses_prior`, `moves_cross_prior`) in `machining2d::arc_cross` and re-exported them internally ([arc_cross.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_cross.rs), [mod.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs)).
- Scaled `microlift::link_at` lift heights strictly below the nearest earlier horizontal `Feed` cut plane above `z`, probed candidate links against prior `Feed` moves, promoted crossing low links to `high: true` down-only links when clear, and fell back to a `hop_z` rapid plus `Plunge` retract when even `down` crosses or the gap is `<= 0.02 mm` ([microlift.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs)).
- Protected 3-D offset shells by probing `descent::push_helix` against posted `b.moves()` (re-placing around `along_pass`/`dive_room` or calling `fallback` when no bore clears) and hopping over any `level_ctx::feed_leg` chord that crosses a prior `Feed` move at shared depth or Z band ([descent.rs](crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs), [level_ctx.rs](crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_ctx.rs)).
- Added unit and integration pinning tests ([entry.rs](crates/motion/src/entry.rs), [microlift.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs), [pocket3d_mask_edge.rs](crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_mask_edge.rs)) and recorded the unattended design choices ([2237-pocket3d-mask-crossing.md](docs/decisions/2237-pocket3d-mask-crossing.md)).

## Cause

- `helix_about` snapped its last half-turn to `lattice(z1)` (`-0.45` vs `-0.44999999999999996`), leaving a 1-ULP ramp that overlapped the next level's descending helix (`min_hi - max_lo = 5.55e-17 > 0`).

## What changed
- Added `operation::extend_to_loop_in(world, setup, picks)` in `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_picks.rs` and re-exported it in `crates/app/src/operation/mod.rs`.
- Replaced `model::transform_of` with `setup_align::pose_in(world, &e, setup)` inside `extend_to_loop_in`. Face normals now rotate into the setup's part-alignment frame, matching `OpFrame::pose_in_setup` in `selection.rs`.
- Updated `operation::extend_to_loop(world, picks)` to call `extend_to_loop_in` with `setup::active(world)`, matching the viewport's `view_pose`.
- Updated `boundary_draft::extend` in `crates/ui/src/boundary_draft.rs` and `edge_pick::take_loop` in `crates/ui/src/edge_pick.rs` to pass the operation's `setup` to `extend_to_loop_in`.
- Added decision note `docs/decisions/2216-extend-to-loop-setup-align.md`.

## Cause
`boundary_picks::extend_to_loop` read `model::transform_of(world, &e)` and ignored the setup's `part_alignment`. Pure Z turns and 180-degree X/Y flips keep `|n.z|` unchanged (`|-n.z| == |n.z|`), so they matched by coincidence. A 90-degree flip onto a side or a free angle tilts Z, so `extend_to_loop` picked the model-frame horizontal face instead of the setup-frame horizontal face.

## Tests

Actual shell and GPU viewport captures from the same fixture, with Setup2 active and its part alignment rotated 90° about X. Before captures temporarily restore the old `model::transform_of` lookup; after captures use this PR head. The old lookup selects the vertical model-top face. title: fix(ui): show a progress overlay over the viewport while a toolpath generates
body: #2257: while an operation generates its toolpath, the viewport shows no progress. The cause is that generation ran in the frame, on the UI thread. Thus no frame painted until the job ended. ## What changed - **Generation on a worker** (native window only). `GenerateOperation` already had a seam between the world reads and the pure work (M5.3 B). That seam is now public as `StagedGeneration`: - `StagedGeneration::new` reads the world on the UI thread. - `StagedGeneration::finish` runs the generator, the verification and the stamp on a worker thread. - The result lands through the same undoable `GenerateOperation` as before. The generators, the verify check and the post gate do not change. - **The overlay** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/gen_overlay.rs`) lies at the top centre of the viewport while a job runs. The navigation strip at the bottom and the view cube stay clear. It shows: - the label of the operation; - "(2 of 5)" when more generations wait in the queue; - the elapsed time and an activity bar (the generators report no fraction); - a `Cancel generation` button. - **Stale results are discarded.** The user can edit, undo or delete while the worker runs. A result lands only while its operation and its cached path are the same as at staging (`GenerateOperation::still_current`). If not, the status line says: `generation of X discarded: the operation changed while it generated - generate it again`. - **Cancel** drops the result and the queue. The old toolpath stays. A worker that runs finishes in the background, and its result is ignored. - **New and Open** drop a running generation. A result for the old document never lands in the new one. - **The viewport takes no press inside the overlay.** A click on Cancel is not also a viewport pick. - **Only the window turns it on** (`State::gen_jobs.background`). Tests, headless runs, scripts and MCP keep the synchronous path. `State::settle` waits for the worker. The browser has no threads: a failed spawn runs the job in place, as the import worker does. - **Repaint:** the shell asks for a repaint every 50 ms only while a job runs or waits (`view_pass::state_redraw_delay`). A frame with no job does no more work than before (#2238). - **No world search in a frame.** The job finds its operation entity one time, when it starts. Each frame reads the label from that entity (`model::live_operation_label`, which checks that the entity is alive). A rename shows at once. A deleted operation shows its name. - Decision record: `docs/decisions/2257-generate-progress-overlay.md`. ## What it looks like Rendered headless from the seeded shell at 1280x800 (a throwaway test, not in the branch). The images are below. - Before: while `Contour1` generates, the viewport shows nothing. - After: the overlay at the top centre, with the operation name, the elapsed time, the activity bar and `Cancel generation`. **Before** (the viewport while `Contour1` generates): **After** (the overlay at the top centre): ## Tests New pinning tests: - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/generate_progress.rs` (structural; the result comes through a channel that the test holds, so no frame races a real generator): - `the_overlay_names_the_running_operation_and_goes_when_it_lands`: the overlay text `Generating Contour1 - ...` is over the viewport, and the Cancel button is there while the job runs. The two go when the job lands. - `a_refusal_ends_the_overlay_and_keeps_its_message` - `cancel_ends_the_overlay_and_drops_the_result`: a click on Cancel ends the overlay. The status says that the generation is cancelled. No history entry is written. - `a_result_for_an_operation_edited_meanwhile_is_discarded`: the edit stays, and the old result writes nothing. - `background_generation_lands_the_same_toolpath`: a real worker run through `settle`. - `the_overlay_text_counts_a_batch` - `one_search_for_each_job_and_a_rename_shows_without_another`: 10 frames and 100 progress reads do one name search. A rename shows in the overlay with no new search. - `a_deleted_operation_shows_its_name_and_no_dead_entity_is_read`: the overlay shows `Contour1` after a delete. Without the `is_alive` check, the test process stops (0xc0000409). - `crates/app/tests/generate_staged.rs`: - `staged_then_finished_lands_what_the_one_shot_command_lands`: the same path either way. - `a_result_is_stale_after_an_edit_a_generation_or_a_delete` Gates on 08022981: - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (222 steps): green, with two exceptions. Neither comes from this change: - `app suites: wire_tool` does not compile on main. That is #2244 (`CuttingRow` gained `stepdown` and `stepover`). - `ui suites: lib`: three tests in `setup_picks_disarm` failed one time. They pass alone. The same suite on a clean `upstream/main` worktree fails 1 of 3 runs at `--test-threads=16` (`setup_picks_disarm`, `setup_mount_pages`). Thus the failures are timing failures on main. - `generate_progress` (6) and `generate_staged` (2): green after the last layout change. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --bins --test generate_staged -- -D warnings`: clean. `--all-targets` stops at `wire_tool` (#2244). - No snapshot PNG changed. Review fix on 43b789ed (label read from the entity): - `generate_progress` (8): green. - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` at `--test-threads=16`: 1025 passed, 0 failed. - `generate_staged` (2): green. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - `model.rs` gets 7 lines (`live_operation_label`). The file was 482 lines before this change. The helper is next to `operation_label`, because the UI crate does no raw world call. ## Not exercised - No hand test in the real window on a long job. The structural tests drive the same `viewport_panel` code through the harness. - `RegenerateAll` (the batch fix of the stale operations) stays synchronous. Its rounds write the world between rounds, so it does not split at one seam. It shows no overlay. The overlay's "n of m" counts single generations that wait in the queue. - The browser build was not run. Its generation stays synchronous through the spawn fallback. title: fix(ui): cache pick highlight geometry and batch stroke draws
body:
## What changed

- Added thread-local weak lookup indexes (`resolve_chain_arc`, `patches_arc`, `patch_rings_arc`) in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature/index.rs`.
- Removed per-triangle heap allocations in `digest_of` and hoisted lattice construction in `patches` and `patch_rings` inside `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs`.
- Added `SHARED_FEATURES_CACHE` (`Weak<[Triangle]>`, cap 32) in `crates/app/src/model/geometry.rs` so repeated `features_of` reads skip `digest_of`.
- Added non-cloning `toolpath_nonempty` and `toolpath_warning_count` in `crates/app/src/model.rs`, used them in `operation::stamp::status_of` and `browser_tree::op_row`, and added `History::revision_token` in `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`.
- Switched `Arc<Features>` lookups in `crates/app/src/operation/{selection.rs, stitch.rs}`, `crates/app/src/pick/{face.rs, feature_sel.rs}`, and `crates/ui/src/{edge_pick.rs, interact.rs, state.rs}` to `*_arc` helpers.
- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight.rs` (`HighlightCache`) to resolve selected, hovered, and row-hovered outlines once per state change.
- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight_mesh.rs` to tessellate each highlight layer into one cached `egui::Shape::Mesh` in `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel`.
- Added `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs` and `crates/ui/src/panel_cache.rs` on `State` to cache world vertices, cutting regions and outlines, toolpath overlay lines, non-transient `world::Scene` plus digest, Geometry chips, 3-2-1 datum checks, selection account, unresolved notes, operation status banners, and browser operation rows.
- Review fix (`b654e0502`): `WorldVertsEntry` in `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs` keeps a `Weak<[Triangle]>` of the source facets, not a raw address. A released source cannot match, and its address cannot be reused while the entry holds the `Weak`. Dead entries are pruned on each lookup.
- Added architecture decision record in `docs/decisions/2201-highlighter-frame-perf.md`.

## Cause

- On models with many chains or facets, `features_of` re-hashed triangle buffers and `resolve_chain` re-walked and split chains repeatedly during frame, highlight, and panel queries.
- `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel` emitted two individual `Shape::LineSegment` shapes per projected segment per frame.
- `world::collect`, `toolpath_lines`, `stamp::status_of`, `browser_tree::op_row`, `op_page`, and `geo_page` rebuilt and cloned vertices, outlines, warnings, and toolpaths on every frame even when inputs stayed unchanged.

## Screenshots

Real `1280x720` shell and `View3D` renders. Before is `1f15f98e7` (the PR base). After is `b654e0502`. The images are only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.

| Welded face | ![Before welded face](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/3441230386b638c8bfd4478b8cb22b908ff25aad/2256/before-welded-face.png) | ![After welded face](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/3441230386b638c8bfd4478b8cb22b908ff25aad/2256/after-welded-face.png) |

## Tests

  - `three_selected_edge_pieces_draw_as_a_single_batched_highlight` (red on unchanged code)

  - `selected_welded_patch_draws_as_batched_highlight_with_single_build` (red on unchanged code)

  - Both fail when the key goes back to the raw `facets_ptr` address. Both pass on the fix.
- Geometry unit tests in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature/index.rs` (`2 passed; 0 failed` in `camcraft-geometry`):
  - `resolve_chain_arc_matches_uncached_for_chains_runs_singletons_and_missing`

- Mutation 1: restoring `crates/ui/src/pick_ink.rs` from `upstream/main` failed all 4 `highlight_perf` pins (`0 passed; 4 failed`, `3 pieces must draw as 1-2 batched shapes, got 180`). Restoring the fix passed all 4 pins (`4 passed; 0 failed`).

Select and export llvm-ar for macOS wasm builds when AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown is unset.
Try PATH, Homebrew LLVM, then the active Rust toolchain.
Preserve explicit overrides and Linux behavior.
Refuse missing tools before downloads and name both installation options.

## Cause
Apple archive tools cannot index the flecs wasm objects.
The resulting archive leaves the linker with undefined symbols.

Run python3 web/test-wasm-ar.py: all seven cases pass with /bin/bash.
The PATH, Homebrew, Rust llvm-tools and missing-tool pins failed before the fix.
Restoring upstream code made those four pins fail again.
Restoring the fix made all seven pass.
The cases also check child-process export, paths with spaces, explicit overrides and Linux.
Run cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main: green, with no Rust tests selected.
Run /bin/bash -n web/build-app-wasm.sh: green.
Clippy does not apply because no Rust crate changed.

None.

The traced playback worker now cuts the whole program one time when the transport starts. It keeps keyframes of the cut stock at a fixed stride. After that, a jump forward or back restores the keyframe at or before the playhead and cuts at most one stride. The program is not cut again during playback.

- `crates/sim/src/play_keys.rs`: `Precalc` state and the checkpoint store, with byte accounting and thinning shared by precalculation and live seeks after cancellation (512 MiB default budget, at most 1024 keyframes, at least 64 moves apart initially).
- `crates/sim/src/play_precalc.rs`: begin/step orchestration, checkpoint policy and the calculation loop through the `Playback` seam. `Keyframes::restores` is the one seek law for `FieldPlay::seek` and the worker.
- `crates/sim/src/play_precalc_mailbox.rs`: progress and cancellation state, with caller-provided stop and elapsed-time bindings.
- `crates/app/src/stock_play_precalc.rs`, `stock_play_worker_precalc.rs`: thin adapters for the existing `FieldPlay` and `PlayWorker` APIs. App retains document gathering, thread lifetime, wakeups, clock binding and frame publication. It re-exports the sim API where needed.
- `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`, `stock_play_worker.rs`: a seek restores a keyframe that is more than one stride ahead, not only one behind. A `moves_cut` counter measures the replay law.
- `crates/ui/src/actions.rs`: the transport starts the worker with the calculation.
- `crates/ui/src/play_precalc.rs` (new), `egui_app/shell.rs`: a line under the transport shows the progress and a Cancel button. A stopped calculation shows "incomplete" with the reason.
- `docs/decisions/2181-sim-precalc.md`: the design and the dropped options.

The stamp is `doc_version`. Each command retires the worker and frees its keyframes (an operation delete included). The keyframes are display only. The Deviate verdict and the post gate do not read them.

## Readings

Release, dense face (100 mm block, stepover 0.5, stepdown 0.5, `DEFAULT_TEXELS`), `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`:

- 4268 moves, 68 keyframes, stride 64
- keyframe memory 444940288 bytes (424 MiB, under the 512 MiB budget)
- calculation time 23.9 s

During the calculation the sheet stands and the line shows the progress. Follow-up #2193 serves frames during the calculation. Follow-up #2194 lowers the keyframe memory.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs`:
- `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position` (bit-identical cut layer at each move, forward and back jumps mixed)
- `a_jump_after_the_calculation_cuts_at_most_one_stride` (no new full calculation)
- `the_keyframes_stay_within_the_memory_budget`
- `a_stopped_calculation_leaves_exact_keyframes_and_cuts_the_rest_live`
- `the_worker_calculates_first_then_replays_and_the_post_gate_is_unchanged` (`posting::verification_gate` is equal before and after)
- `a_cancelled_calculation_is_incomplete_by_name_and_playback_goes_on`
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` (ignored, heavy lane, the reading above)

`crates/sim/tests/play_precalc.rs` (#2192 review, finding 4):
- `domain_calculation_resets_cuts_and_reports_the_bounded_store`
- `domain_mailbox_cancel_preserves_partial_checkpoints_and_names_the_end`
- `domain_mailbox_reports_progress_and_uses_the_owners_stop_and_clock`
- `a_seek_restores_behind_or_more_than_a_stride_ahead`

`crates/ui/src/play_precalc_tests.rs`:
- `the_readout_says_progress_and_incomplete_and_nothing_when_done`
- `an_edit_of_the_operation_retires_the_stored_calculation`

## Gate

Fix round at head 5d929ae (finding 4 again; the local commit 738492b of the earlier round was never pushed, so this round makes the move again on the pushed branch):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --test play_precalc --test play_keys`: 4 + 4 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test stock_play --test stock_play_precalc --test stock_play_partial --test stock_sim_document`: 7, 7 (1 ignored, the heavy reading), 3, 9 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib precalc`: 6 pass (the transport row and readout tests). No ui file changed in this round.
- Clippy with `-D warnings`: sim all targets; app lib and the four suites above; ui lib and tests.
- Mutation: with the keyframe offer removed from `play_precalc::step`, two of the new sim pins fail. The restored source passes.
- Not run: the quick tier (over one hour on sim branches), the full app and ui suites, the heavy lanes.

## Screenshots

Headless render of the real shell (test harness, 1280x720), captured in the earlier fix round and preserved from image commit `a94079e073ac7e38f14569eca085dec7a903e17a`. The before image shows the transport before precalculation. The after images show the reviewed transport change. These PNGs are hosted only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

Before: the transport row has no precalculation line.

![before](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-2192/before-transport.png>)

After, while the calculation runs: the progress text and the Cancel button.

![after running](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-2192/after-running.png>)

After, when Cancel stopped the calculation: the "incomplete" text with the reason. There is no Cancel button.

![after incomplete](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-2192/after-incomplete.png>)

## Not exercised

- The windowed app was not started. The screenshots come from the headless test harness render of the real shell.
- The reading uses one large fixture only.

## Overlap

#2182 changes other hunks of `crates/ui/src/actions.rs` (status strings). The two PRs do not stack.

Changelog: Simulation playback calculates the stock removal one time before it plays, then replays it, so a jump on the timeline does not lag. A line under the transport shows the progress and can cancel the calculation.

Effort: high (issue label effort:max; an Opus worker of the high tier works it by the maintainer's order; no escalation)

- Added **Do not touch** protected faces, patches, and edge chains plus standoff **Clearance** (`>= 0.0` mm, default `0.0`) to `AreaControls` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`, `area.rs`).
- Separated `has_boundary_edits()` from `is_default()` so empty protection preserves legacy toolpaths, boundary clipping, and generation stamps (`op_stamp` hashes `camcraft-do-not-touch-v1` only when protection is active).
- Added independent 3D full-tool keep-out generation and swept verification in `crates/sim/src/verify/` (`avoid.rs`, `avoid_poly.rs`, `avoid_links.rs`, `swept.rs`, `probe.rs`, `Warning::AvoidHit`), checking flutes, shank, and holder against `clearance + max(stock_to_leave, 0)` and elevating obstructed rapid traverses.

Review-fix head: `928c878dbcdae917f1de9523213caeb1874b451d`. Merged `upstream/main` at `a49322b9c0c049bd0b3b2d1dea855de6087ac64b`; kept the cutting-data and Weldon holder descriptions. Both new commits carry `Fixes #2055`.

- Split work-offset frame classification (`OffsetFrame::Yaw` vs tilted `OffsetFrame::Rotated`) in `crates/app/src/posting_wcs_rotation.rs`.

title: feat(app)!: place a DXF profile on a setup's stock - Sketch entity, ImportDxf, import_dxf MCP tool
body:
Stacked on #2106 (sketch chaining, issue 1861). Merge #2106 first. This branch now merges upstream `main` and keeps both project modules and the breakthrough fields from #1557.

## What changed

A DXF drawing is now a profile that the user places on the stock of a setup. It is not a model. This follows the scope change of the maintainer on issue 1862 (2026-11-15).

- **`Sketch` component** (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, registered in `register_schema`). It holds the setup and the shared drawing data. The entity has no `Facets`, and `model::is_model` is false for it. No 3D solid tool reads it as a mesh.
- **`camcraft_geometry::sketch_data::SketchData`**: the primitives in mm, the layer names, the source units, the join tolerance, the chains of issue 1861 and the import summary. The chains are always made from the stored primitives.
- **Placement** (`crates/app/src/sketch.rs`): the `Location` of a profile is relative to the top face of the stock of its setup, at the stock origin. A profile has Z 0 and a turn about the face normal only. A moved or resized stock carries the profile.
- **`ImportDxf::new(world, setup, path, options)`** (undoable). It gets the setup as an argument (`None`: the active setup). It refuses at construction: a setup with no stock, an unknown setup, a file that is not `.dxf`, a malformed DXF, a drawing with nothing to place, a name in use. A file with no `$INSUNITS` (absent or 0) and no unit from the caller gives the typed `CommandError::DxfUnitsMissing { width, height }`.
- **`MoveSketch::new(world, name, x, y, angle_deg)`** (undoable): the move and the turn on the stock face.
- **`DeleteEntity`** restores a profile on undo. **`SelectEntity`** works on a profile. **`MoveModel`** and **`DeleteSetup`** refuse a profile by name.
- **Virtual model reference** (`crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`): it is derived from the world when a setup has a placed profile and the document has no part. Nothing is stored for it.
- **Project file**: entity kind `sketch` with a `sketch` key; `PROJECT_VERSION` 66 -> 67. The chains are made again on load.
- **MCP**: `import_dxf` and `move_dxf_profile`. `get_job` lists `profiles`, gives each setup a `model_reference`, and gives an operation on a profile `checks_against`. **Script**: `cam.importDxf(path, { setup, units, join_tol, name })`.
- `docs/decisions/1862-sketch-profile.md` records the design of the virtual reference: what it is in the ECS, what the project file stores, and which checks read it.

## How each point of the scope change is met

1. A profile is not a model: `is_model` is false, `model_entities` does not list it, `get_job` lists it under `profiles`.
2. A setup with a stock and no model is legal: the tests make a sheet stock, place the profile and add an operation.
3. The `Sketch` belongs to the setup. Its `Location` is relative to the stock top face at the stock origin. `MoveSketch` moves and turns it on that face.
4. `ImportDxf` gets the setup. Undo removes the profile. The MCP tool and the script verb get the same argument.
5. The virtual model reference is `sketch_model::of(world, setup)`. The source door of the operation commands accepts a profile as a source. The model-height diagnostic names the reference. `sketch_model::model_loaded` is the question for the operation pages of issue 1863. The reference has no facets.
6. No check passes silently. An operation on a profile states what it is checked against (the stock and the chains of the profile). A kind that needs a solid model refuses a profile by name. A 3D kind in a setup with a virtual reference refuses by name. Generation of an operation on a profile refuses by name (see the open questions).
7. The decision file is in this PR.

## Project file version

This PR writes **version 67**. Current upstream `main` writes version 66 for the trunnion schema from #1962. Profiles take the next version. Main's trunnion fields, v65-to-v66 migration and earlier steps stay intact, and the v66-to-v67 profile step needs no data rewrite. Stated `controller_rtcp: false` and trunnion data remain intact, as do tilt bases, earlier cutting-data rows and breakthrough values. A v62 file still loads through the earlier migration (`a_v62_file_steps_up_unchanged`). Tests check v63 breakthrough and v64 cutting-data files through load, save as v67, and load again. The v65 tilt pins retain legacy basis 0 and basis 1 through load, save, and reload. The new v66 trunnion pin checks the stated machine data through load, save, and reload. The profile and rest payloads also survive a v67 save and load.

## Open design questions

These need a decision of the maintainer. This PR does the part that is specified and does not guess the rest.

1. **Toolpath from the chains.** The added "Done means" says that the setup "accepts a 2D operation on the sketch chains". This PR accepts the operation at each command door (create, paste, retarget, retype, move to a setup). It does not generate a toolpath from the chains: issue 1864 has that work (chain picks, side per chain, checks without a mesh). Until then, generation refuses by name and says what the operation is checked against. Is that the correct split, or must #1862 also generate?
2. **Top of Model and Bottom of Model on a virtual reference.** A reference with no solid has no top and no bottom. This PR refuses these heights by name (the text tells the user to use a stock or fixed height). The alternative is to give them a value, for example the stock top and the stock bottom. That changes cut depths, so it is not decided here.
3. **"The stock origin".** This PR reads it as the origin of the stock entity. For a box and a cylinder that is the centre in XY. The alternative is a corner of the stock or the WCS origin.
4. **Which kinds take a profile.** This PR admits the 2D milling, plasma and wire EDM sections. Drilling (holes from DXF circles), turning and sinker EDM refuse a profile by name. Is that the correct set?
5. **`MoveSketch` and not `MoveModel`.** The issue body said `MoveModel`. A profile has a face placement (X, Y, angle), and `MoveModel` writes a world placement and carries the stock. This PR adds `MoveSketch`, and `MoveModel` refuses a profile by name.
6. **A profile that is larger than the stock, or off its edge,** is not refused at placement. Issue 1864 has the check of the chains against the stock.

`crates/geometry/tests/sketch_data.rs` (9): units and scale, the missing-units refusal with extents, an unsupported unit code, an empty drawing, stored parts read back, arc bounds, and invalid stored summary counts.

title: feat(ai): provider HTTP clients, keychain keys and offline-only mode
body:
**New third-party crates - needs the maintainer's decision (`needs-maintainer`):**

| Crate | Version | Licence | Why the workspace's existing deps can't do it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reqwest` | 0.12.28 (default features off, `rustls-tls`) | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | Provides an async HTTP request that cancellation can interrupt. Redirects and environment proxies are disabled. |
| `tokio` | 1.52.3 (`rt`, `time`, `net`, `macros`) | MIT | Runs each request on a current-thread runtime inside the chat worker. Cancellation drops the active request future. |
| `rustls` / `rustls-webpki` / `rustls-pki-types` | 0.23.46 / 0.103.17 / 1.16.0 (via reqwest) | Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT / ISC / MIT OR Apache-2.0 | TLS for the https cloud APIs; no OpenSSL on Linux. |
| `ring` + `untrusted` | 0.17.14 / 0.9.0 (via rustls) | Apache-2.0 AND ISC / ISC | rustls's crypto (C/asm, built by `cc`; no CMake, unlike aws-lc-rs). |
| `webpki-roots` | 1.0.12 | CDLA-Permissive-2.0 | The Mozilla CA roots, so the build needs no system trust store. |
| `keyring` + `keyring-core` | 4.2.0 / 1.0.1 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | Nothing in the tree reaches an OS credential store. |
| keyring stores: `apple-native-keyring-store` (+ `security-framework`), `windows-native-keyring-store`, `zbus-secret-service-keyring-store` (+ `secret-service`) | 1.x | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Secret Service. The Linux store rides the `zbus` 5 **already in the lock** - pure Rust, no `libdbus` build package. |
| RustCrypto `aes`, `cbc`, `cipher`, `hkdf`, `hmac`, `sha2`, `digest`, `subtle`, `zeroize`, ... (via secret-service) | various | MIT OR Apache-2.0 (`subtle` BSD-3-Clause) | Secret Service session encryption. |

`url` 2.5 was **already in Cargo.lock** and is now a direct dependency of `camcraft-app` (endpoint parsing with the same URL parser reqwest uses). All new crates are under `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]` of `camcraft-app` only; the browser build links none of them. Notices added to `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`. The review fix replaces blocking `ureq` with `reqwest` and a current-thread `tokio` runtime so cancellation interrupts active requests. Considered and dropped: detached blocking requests (they keep the socket and worker alive), `native-tls` (OpenSSL headers on Linux), keyring's dbus store (vendored libdbus C build) - see `docs/decisions/1945-ai-provider-clients.md`.

## What changed

- **`camcraft_app::ai`** (new, `crates/app/src/ai/`):
  - `endpoint` - URL parse (WHATWG `url`; user info, query and fragment refused), loopback test (`localhost`, 127/8, `::1`, IPv4-mapped), `admit` (offline-only reaches loopback alone; plain `http://` off the machine is refused, key or not), `admit_addrs` (the resolver's half).
  - `presets` - Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (GPT and Codex), Gemini `generateContent` (all `https://`); Ollama `http://localhost:11434/v1`, Unsloth Studio `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`, LM Studio `http://localhost:1234/v1`, llama.cpp `llama-server` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (`--jinja` named in the label).
  - `wire` - the request path and body per provider. Tool-call envelopes are echoed in each provider's own shape (Anthropic content blocks, Chat `tool_calls` message, Responses `output` items incl. reasoning, Gemini content incl. `thoughtSignature`); consecutive tool results merge into one Anthropic user message / one Gemini turn. Model ids are checked so they cannot add a query or climb the Gemini path. Fallback (prompt-JSON / Q&A) payloads go into the system prompt with no tools.
  - `probe` - Ollama `/api/show` capabilities -> tools / vision / fallback mode.
  - `secret` - `ApiKey` has no `Display` and a redacted `Debug`, refuses control characters (no header injection); lookup is the env var (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) first, then the keychain.
  - `http` (native only) - the client. `admit` runs before anything resolves; the agent's resolver refuses non-loopback addresses when offline-only or plain http; **no redirects followed**, **no proxy from the environment**, connect/total timeouts, auth only in headers (`x-api-key`, `Authorization: Bearer`, `x-goog-api-key`), errors carry the host, status and the provider's message - never the key.
  - `keychain` (native only) - `load` / `store` / `forget` under the service `camcraft-ai`.
- **`prefs.json`** gains `aiOfflineOnly` (written only when on); `ViewPrefs` has no field that could hold a key.
- **AI Chat dock** (`crates/ui`): native builds use the new `transport_http::HttpTransport` (presets map to the endpoints above; the key comes from env/keychain or the step is refused by name; an Ollama model without the `tools` capability is refused by name in the native-tools preset, pointing at the Prompt-JSON / Q&A presets). The "Offline only" switch is restored from and saved to `prefs.json`. The browser build keeps the offline-only `DefaultTransport` (now `cfg(wasm32)`).

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/ai_http.rs` against a fake loopback HTTP server (no real key: a fixed placeholder sent only to 127.0.0.1): `anthropic_messages_wire_format`, `openai_chat_completions_wire_format`, `openai_responses_wire_format`, `gemini_generate_content_wire_format`, `local_runtimes_send_no_auth_header`, `ollama_capability_probe`, `offline_only_blocks_every_non_loopback_host_before_a_socket` (every cloud preset plus TEST-NET / private / IPv6 hosts refused in < 500 ms, plus the resolver check), `plain_http_off_this_machine_is_refused`, `redirects_are_not_followed_and_errors_never_carry_the_key`. 9/9 pass.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs::offline_only_survives_and_the_file_stores_zero_keys` (the file's keys are exactly the known five; no "key"/"token"/"secret"/"password"/"bearer").
- Unit tests in `ai::endpoint`, `ai::presets`, `ai::secret`, `ai::wire`, `ai::probe`, and `transport_http::every_panel_preset_has_an_endpoint`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (fell back to batch: Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock changed): geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app (incl. `ai_http`, `view_prefs`) and ui suites all **ok** (35.5 min). Clippy `-D warnings` FAILS only on `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` `MIN_LABEL_PX` never used - pre-existing on upstream main since PR #2095, tracked in #2104 / PR #2111; no other lint in the touched crates.
- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (with `web/build-app-wasm.sh`'s wasi sysroot and flecs patch): **Finished** clean; the only warnings are pre-existing unused imports in `ai_chat/worker.rs` (untouched here).

## Not exercised

- No call to a real provider or a real local runtime (no key in tests, no network in tests).
- The OS keychain itself (`keychain::load/store/forget`) is not called by any test - a test would prompt or write the developer's real keychain; the lookup order is pinned with an injected keychain.
- No UI for entering/storing a key yet: keys come from the env vars, or from the keychain if stored by other means (service `camcraft-ai`, account `anthropic`/`openai`/`gemini`). A key-entry field is a follow-up.
- Streaming responses (each step is one complete response, as the dock's worker expects).

Changelog: AI Chat reaches Anthropic, OpenAI (Chat and Responses), Gemini over https and Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio and llama-server on loopback; API keys come only from the environment or the OS keychain; "Offline only" is saved and blocks every non-loopback host in the HTTP client (#1945)

title: test(motion): pin the rest Adaptive raster entry proof and the D/80 load ceiling
body:
**Stacked on #2112** (rest Adaptive, `mkinney:issue/2031-rest-adaptive`, head 71a7fee47). This PR's own change is its last commit (c234093ee); until #2112 merges the diff against main shows #2112's commits too. Merge #2112 first.

## What changed

Tests only (no product code): three pins the M5 review of #2112 found missing.

- **Raster half of the entry proof** - `machining2d::adaptive::rest::tests::the_raster_half_of_the_entry_proof_refuses_on_its_own` (unit test, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/rest/tests.rs`). It hands `Entries` a raster holding a 1 mm pillar that the polygon bound does not hold, then asks for a plunge whose rim would stand 0.2 mm inside the pillar: refused. A plunge clear of the pillar by more than the margin is still proved. Inside the planner the raster comes from the same polygon bound (grown), and the polygon half refuses everything the raster would, so no planner fixture can make the raster refuse on its own. The test therefore works on `Entries` directly.
  - Mutation-checked: removing `&& self.stock.air(p, p, self.footprint)` from `Entries::proved` turns it red, and so does `footprint: 0.0`.
- **Load ceiling on the default D/80 measuring grid** - `on_the_default_measuring_grid_the_load_stays_under_its_documented_ceiling` (`crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`). Optimal x 1.2 (`LOAD_CEILING_D80` in `sim.rs`, with its readings documented), on the climb 3 mm corners and on the conventional 3.5 mm corners with 0.3 mm left.
- **Corner assertion on a fine grid (D/240)** - `on_a_fine_grid_the_corners_read_within_the_planning_margin`. A 26 x 22 pocket with 3.5 mm corners, cut conventionally with 0.3 mm left. On the measuring stock that is 1680 x 1440 cells, under the 4096-cell cap. It must read within the planner's own margin (optimal x 1.05), and every feed stays in the corners.
- `sim.rs`: `Sim::on_grid(region, cell)` and `assert_load_within(reading, slack)`. `assert_load_held` is now `assert_load_within(.., LOAD_SLACK)`.
- `docs/decisions/2113-rest-adaptive-pins.md`.

## Readings (debug, optimal load 14.6% of D)

body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.

The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

title: feat(tools)!: cutting data by work material - Unknown default row, stepdown/stepover, stock material
body:
## What changed

Tool cutting data by work material (#2015, part of #2007):

- **`Unknown` row.** Every tool's cutting data now holds an `Unknown` row (file word `unknown`; in code `CuttingRow::material == None`). It is what the tool runs when no row names the material in force, and the fallback for a row's missing stepdown/stepover. It is derived from the tool's own rpm/feed and stored only when it states something more (other numbers, or a step) - so a new tool has it, every older tool reads its own numbers as it, and plain tools are stored, saved and shown to MCP byte for byte as before. A command that moves the running numbers away from a derived row stores it first. A waterjet (recipes) and an electrode (rpm 0) get none, so a sane tool never turns insane.
- **Stepdown and stepover per row** (mm, optional). They seed an operation's stepdown/stepover only inside an undoable command (quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the feature recognizer, `SetWorkMaterial`, `SetStockMaterial`, retargeting a tool), never on load. Seeded kinds: pocket, adaptive, offset, slot, 3-D pocket, multi-axis rough, face (stepover; stepdown only when staged), 2-D contour (stepdown). A stepover wider than the cutter is refused by tool name.
- **Setup stock material.** New `StockMaterial` component on a setup's stock and the undoable `SetStockMaterial` command (MCP `set_stock_material`, stock page "Material" group). The row is picked by the stock's material, then the document's, then `Unknown`. The tools' running rpm/feed (the posted S word) follow the document material only - a tool is shared by every setup.
- **`.camtools`/project migration.** `PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63 (the issue's "61 to 62" predates #1453's bump). A v62 project loads with each tool's own rpm/feed as its `Unknown` row; nothing it runs moves. `.camtools` reader accepts versions 1, 2 and 3; the writer writes 3 only when a library holds a stated `Unknown` row or a step (otherwise 1, or 2 for left-hand taps, as before). An `Unknown` row that only repeats the tool's own rpm/feed is not written, so plain tools save byte for byte as before (MCP `get_job` output unchanged for them).
- **Tool page.** The "Cutting data by material" group is now a table: Material, Spindle rpm, Feed, Stepdown, Stepover (0 = not stated). The `Unknown` row is first, its material fixed, not removable.
- **Behaviour change, inside a command only:** stating a document material the tool has no row for now runs the tool's `Unknown` row (before: the previous material's numbers stayed). An operation's milling feed still moves only for a row that names the material (#890's rule), so picking a material never overwrites hand-set op feeds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2015-unknown-cutting-row.md` (why `Option<WorkMaterial>` and not a `WorkMaterial::Unknown` variant: `WorkMaterial::row()` indexes the handbook table).

Base: upstream/main (`31f8d03d7`); no file overlap with #2029 (it does not touch `tool_cutting_rows.rs`; both touch `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in different places). Fork synced at the current upstream main for this branch.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/tools/tests/unknown_row.rs` (6): selection order, step fallback, derivation once and only from the running numbers, kinds that get none, refusals (bad steps, `Unknown` twice).
- `crates/app/tests/cutting_unknown_row.rs` (9): `a_new_tool_gets_its_unknown_row_from_its_own_numbers`, `a_v62_project_loads_its_tool_numbers_as_the_unknown_row_with_no_loss`, `a_v1_tool_library_loads_with_the_unknown_row_and_steps_write_v3`, `the_row_is_picked_by_the_stock_then_the_document_then_unknown`, `a_second_setup_stock_material_seeds_only_its_own_operations`, `steps_seed_only_in_commands_and_the_stock_material_round_trips`, `a_project_with_no_new_rows_posts_the_same_s_and_f_words` (posts, re-saves as v62, reloads, re-posts: identical S/F words), `a_stated_stepover_wider_than_the_cutter_is_refused_by_tool_name`, `mcp_sets_the_stock_material_as_one_undo_step`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_material.rs`: the stock page's Material group sits between Shape and Size, and a pick is one undoable `SetStockMaterial`.
- Updated to the new law: `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs` (stating plastics, which has no row, now runs the tool's Unknown row), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs` unit tests (Unknown is shown, never added).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, m5): green on 75031d5f9 (tools, app and ui suites; 6.2 min). Clippy on camcraft-tools, camcraft-app, camcraft-ui: clean (`--all-targets -D warnings`).

## UI before and after

These are headless captures of the real egui controls, rendered with `egui_kittest::Harness::render` on Linux. Before is pre-feature commit `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239`. After is reviewed head `af78aec60436e402c8e026d5bc9521552131bf5a`. The temporary harness called the shipping `cutting_rows` and `stock_page` functions; no UI was mocked. The cutting-data draft has the same Aluminium 6061 row in both captures. The after draft also states stepdown 2 mm and stepover 3 mm. The stock captures use the same seeded document.

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, at commit `b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d`. No capture harness, screenshot, golden, or review evidence was added to this PR branch.

| Control | Before | After |

| Cutting data | ![Cutting data before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-before.png) | ![Cutting data after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-after.png) |
| Stock Material | ![Stock Material before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/stock-material-before.png) | ![Stock Material after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/stock-material-after.png) |

The after table shows the fixed Unknown row, the named material row, and the step fields. The after stock page shows the Material group between Shape and Size. Both render checks passed at each revision (four captures total). This was a headless UI render, not a manual native-window session.

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe G76 J makes LinuxCNC's R1 ladder cut the record's passes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, `g76Grid`: J (first depth) is no longer floored to the grid on its own. LinuxCNC's G76 with `R1` cuts J, 2J, ... with the last pass clamped at K, so the control cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs (g76Why already holds the equal ladder), so J must satisfy (n-1)J < K <= nJ:

- J is the shallower grid rounding (as before) when that keeps the count;
- when the shallower J would add a pass, J is the one grid step up, and never a full grid step over the record's first cut;
- otherwise the record is refused by name: `G76 threading cycle refused - no first depth J on the control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes (K ...)`.

The root keeps its outward rounding. Peak, root, I and K are unchanged.

## Golden change, line by line

`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`, one line:

```
-G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
+G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0315 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
```

What this relies on, from the public LinuxCNC G-code reference (G76): J is the first cut depth, K the full thread depth (diameters here, under G7), and `R1.0` selects constant depth, so each pass goes J deeper than the last and the last pass is clamped at K.
- Old: 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942, then 0.0944 (a 0.0002 in pass) = 4 passes. The record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius).
- New: 0.0315, 0.0630, 0.0944 (clamped) = 3 passes, the record's count. J 0.0315 in is 0.000004 in (0.1 um) over the record's Ø0.8 mm first cut. The root (X + I - K) is the same as before: never deeper than the minor.
- P, Z, I, K, R, Q, H and every other line are unchanged. The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is byte-identical.

The earlier PathPilot Hub 8L sim run of this golden (PR #517 comments) does not cover the new J: **this golden needs a new Hub run** (not done here, no Hub access).

Scan (local script, not committed): realistic records (first depth 0.05-0.5 mm, height 0.3-2 mm, four minor diameters, the stream's lattice) - the old rule mis-stated 2.7% of inch records; the new rule miscounts none and refuses none in either unit. Refusals are reached only by records with many tiny rungs (e.g. 0.15 deep in rungs of 0.012, inch) or a lattice disagreement on the crest.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder.rs`:
- `g76_words_cut_exactly_the_records_passes_in_mm_and_inch` - parses the posted J/K as grid steps, counts ceil(K/J) and asserts it equals both the G33 pass count of the same document and ceil(height / first depth) of its record; asserts J is under one grid step over the record's first cut.
- `g76_refuses_by_name_when_no_grid_j_cuts_the_records_passes` - mm: crest +2 um (inside the lattice allowance) makes K 2.402, refused (J 0.801 would be a full step heavy); inch: 0.15 deep in 0.012 rungs, K 118 steps, no whole J with 12J < 118 <= 13J, refused.

Updated: `a_thread_posts_as_one_g76_block_with_the_option_in_mm_and_inch` (inch line J0.0315, golden regenerated).

Mutation checks (each mutation applied, suites run, file restored and touched):
- delete `if (j < lo) j = lo;` -> both new tests red (and the golden test);
- delete the refusal `return { why: ... }` line -> refusal test red;
- drop the `j <= hi` half of the refusal condition -> refusal test red (inch case);
- drop the `j - jRec < 1` half -> refusal test red (mm case).

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites 5 s, app suites 1648 s - the shared golden pulled every app suite). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder --test lathe_post_tormach_thread -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a PathPilot / LinuxCNC run of the new inch golden; no batch gate (budget).

## Overlaps

- #517 and #518 (G76 on both lathe posts): `git merge-tree` with each branch is clean (#517 changes `g76Why`, this changes `g76Grid`), so not stacked. With #517's finish-allowance rule the record's rung count is still ceil(height / first depth).
- #1667 and #1681 conflict with this on adjacent lines of the same inch golden and `lathe_post_tormach_thread.rs` (their G30 / drive-line changes next to the G76 line): a mechanical keep-both, regenerate the golden at merge.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1619-g76-inch-ladder.md`.

Fork synced at v0.19.0 (branched from upstream/main 058e14ca).

Changelog: Tormach lathe G76 (inch) states a first depth J whose LinuxCNC R1 ladder cuts exactly the verified passes (J0.0315, not 0.0314, on the M12x2 fixture); a record no grid J can state is refused by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1619
